budget.scope: existing web service, existing PostgreSQL instance and 1 GB evidence/cache disk
budget.condition: Verify current provider quote fits the approved cap before mutation; metered traffic/build usage is separate. Do not enable storage autoscaling or add other resources.

preconditions: Final local release gates pass and the exact deploy commit is recorded.
Take and hash an off-host PostgreSQL custom-format dump; inspect it with pg_restore.
Preserve any accessible old evidence before replacing an ephemeral instance; do not claim inaccessible history was recovered.
Obtain explicit approval for the new recurring charges.
Check fresh service/database/disk metadata before applying; stop if resource identity or configuration has changed.

requestsAfterApproval.condition: No existing disk at this mount; otherwise inspect/reuse it without recreating or shrinking it.

acceptance: Database available, no free-plan expiry; PostgreSQL/PostGIS functionality and original inventory still readable.
Explicit pinned deploy reaches live; public /api/health release.commit matches the approved SHA.
Health reports snapshotEvidence.mountVerified=true, durability=mounted_filesystem and no write block.
Retain an explicitly identified evidence/control observation, record its ledger head and raw digest, then restart/redeploy and verify identical bytes/head remain.
Create evidence archive on host with scripts/evidence-backup.js, copy it off host, verify its SHA-256 and restore only into a new isolated directory; verify raw/markdown/PDF and ledger-head readback.
Enable/check provider database backups and prove restoration in a separate PostgreSQL target before accepting disaster recovery.
Record hosted deployment, persistence and recovery receipts; retain later-track hold until all remaining acceptance rows close.
rollback: Redeploy the prior known working commit with the same mounted disk and database.
Never delete/detach the disk, downgrade to ephemeral storage, restore over the live store, or delete the database as rollback.
A paid-to-free database reversal is not assumed possible; retain storage and stop for operator review if cost expectations change.
